item.title: Two giant pandas set off from Chengdu for 10-year stay at Zoo Atlanta
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-27
This photo taken on Sept. 27, 2026 shows a chartered flight carrying a pair of giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, at Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport in southwest China's Sichuan Province. The giant panda pair departed for Zoo Atlanta in the U.S. at 2:55 a.m. Sunday, kicking off their 10-year stay at the zoo. (Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding/Handout via Xinhua) CHENGDU, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- A pair of Chinese giant pandas departed for Zoo Atlanta in the United States on a chartered flight at 2:55 a.m. Sunday, kicking off their 10-year stay at the zoo, according to the National Forestry and Grassland Administration. Before their departure from Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport in southwest China's Sichuan Province, the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding held a farewell ceremony for Ping Ping, a sturdy yet agile male panda born on March 17, 2020, and Fu Shuang, a chubby, vivacious female born on Oct. 18, 2020. To ensure the pandas' safety and comfort during their trans-Pacific journey, the Chinese team drew up a detailed transportation plan and prepared ample supplies of fresh bamboo shoots, bamboo, apples and emergency medications, officials with the administration said. Before the journey, the pandas also underwent transport acclimation training to help reduce anxiety and stress. Senior veterinarians and keepers from the United States are accompanying the pandas, monitoring their health in real time and attending to their dietary and other needs during the journey. The Chinese side has also arranged for two teams of veterinarians and keepers to travel to Zoo Atlanta in advance to make the necessary preparations. During the flight, cabin temperature and humidity will be maintained within a comfortable range for the pandas. Upon arrival in Atlanta, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang will undergo quarantine and health checks. Chinese veterinarians and keepers will stay at the zoo throughout the quarantine period to care for the pandas and help them adapt to their new surroundings through acclimation and behavioral training. To create a healthy and comfortable living environment for the pandas, Chinese experts and Zoo Atlanta have held multiple online and in-person meetings since December 2025 to discuss the upgrading of the zoo's panda facilities. Chinese experts provided technical guidance on facilities and equipment, husbandry and management, food supplies and health care. Zoo Atlanta has adopted the recommendations and carried out the renovations as planned. The upgraded facilities feature a significantly expanded indoor exhibit area, new enrichment features such as climbing structures, rock platforms and a pool, and an upgraded monitoring system that provides more comprehensive real-time information on conditions inside and outside the enclosures. In mid-September, Chinese experts conducted an on-site inspection and acceptance check of the upgraded facilities. In terms of food supplies, Zoo Atlanta can obtain a variety of edible bamboo locally, as the area's climate is similar to that of Chengdu. Fresh bamboo can be harvested year-round, ensuring an adequate supply for the two pandas, Chinese experts said. China and Zoo Atlanta have conducted cooperative research on panda conservation for more than two decades and made significant progress. The two sides have jointly carried out more than 30 research projects and published over 50 academic papers, making a number of technological breakthroughs in panda breeding and cub rearing, behavioral studies, and disease prevention and control. During their cooperation, the two sides successfully bred seven pandas, representing a high level of achievement in international panda breeding cooperation. The two sides have also carried out extensive academic and people-to-people exchanges, helping facilitate mutual understanding and friendship between the Chinese and American peoples. ■ Staff members transfer giant panda Ping Ping at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, Sept. 26, 2026. item.title: Chinese choreographer blends street dance with traditional Chinese cultural elements
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-27
Fang Zhenghua (R) instructs Homies dancers at Dancehome studio in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, June 13, 2026. Fang Zhenghua, a post-90s choreographer, has participated in the production of a series of eye-catching dancing performances, including a show featuring dancers and humanoid robots at the opening ceremony of the 48th WorldSkills Competition. For Fang, street dance has never been merely a passing trend. Fang's love for street dance began at the age of 13, when he first learned popular dance moves from television. That early fascination soon grew into a lifelong pursuit, driving him to explore new possibilities on stage. A big fan of Chinese martial arts novels since childhood, Fang has integrated Sichuan Opera face-changing techniques, traditional Kung Fu movements and other distinct Chinese cultural elements into his choreography. In March 2025, Fang and Homies, a street dance team of his studio Dancehome, won third place at the VIBE Dance Competition with their work "Sword and Qi in Sichuan." This was the first time a Chinese team had claimed an award in the competition's 30-year history. His team has also collaborated with domestic humanoid robot developers, staging performances that showcase China's technological advances. Nearly 20 years of dedication has brought Fang to stages around the world. "When we compete abroad, our goal is not just to show the world how Chinese dancers move," he said. "We want them to see a rich, diverse China through every step we take." item.title: Moments in Motion | President Xi's Washington Time
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-27
"I am visiting the United States at President Trump's invitation to carry on our friendship, expand cooperation and promote the well-being of both our peoples," Chinese President Xi Jinping said at a White House welcoming ceremony on Thursday. The Chinese leader's state visit to the United States, from Wednesday to Friday, drew worldwide attention. Fighter jets flew over the airport and the White House in tribute, and 21-gun salutes were fired at the airport as Xi arrived and departed. The special arrangements reflected the importance Trump attached to Xi's trip. A number of new consensuses were reached during the visit. The two sides also agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. Produced by Xinhua Global Service■

item.title: PLA conducts joint naval-air exercise around China's Huangyan Dao
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-27
BEIJING, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- Naval and air units of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Southern Theater Command conducted a joint training exercise in the waters and airspace around China's Huangyan Dao in the South China Sea on Sunday. A statement from the command said the exercise is a necessary operation taken in response to the acts by certain countries that have undermined regional peace and stability. The training exercise aims to test and enhance the combat capabilities to safeguard China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, the statement said. Focusing on realistic training subjects such as reconnaissance and early warning, rapid maneuver, and joint search and rescue, the exercise effectively honed the troops' naval-air coordination, rapid support and win-by-system capabilities, according to the command. It pledged that forces of the command will stay on high alert at all times and resolutely safeguard China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests. On the same day, the China Coast Guard (CCG) conducted drills on maritime rights protection, law enforcement, and management and control in the waters near Huangyan Dao. The CCG's drills focused on operations such as boarding and inspection, interdiction of intrusion, and forced towing, said Jiang Lue, spokesperson for the CCG, in a statement. The CCG will step up efforts in rights protection, law enforcement, and management and control in the waters near Huangyan Dao, and resolutely safeguard China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, Jiang said. China has sovereignty over Nanhai Zhudao (the South China Sea Islands), consisting of Dongsha Qundao (the Dongsha Islands), Xisha Qundao (the Xisha Islands), Zhongsha Qundao (the Zhongsha Islands) and Nansha Qundao (the Nansha Islands). Huangyan Dao is located in the Zhongsha Islands. China has historic rights in the South China Sea. China also has internal waters, territorial sea, contiguous zone, exclusive economic zone and continental shelf, based on Nanhai Zhudao. Nanhai Zhudao have long been widely recognized by the international community as part of China's territory. ■

item.title: Full text: Address by Chinese VP at the high-level dialogue on the fifth anniversary of the Global Development Initiative
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-27
UNITED NATIONS, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Vice President Han Zheng on Friday delivered a speech at the high-level dialogue on the fifth anniversary of the Global Development Initiative. The following is the full text of the speech: Remarks by H.E. Han Zheng Vice President of the People's Republic of China At the High-Level Dialogue on the Fifth Anniversary of The Global Development Initiative New York, September 25, 2026 Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Dear Friends, Welcome to the High-Level Dialogue on the Fifth Anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI). In September 2021, President Xi Jinping put forward the GDI at the 76th Session of the United Nations General Assembly. Five years on, thanks to his personal commitment and the concerted efforts of all parties, the GDI has been translated from a Chinese vision and proposal into collective global action, and from a development blueprint into concrete cooperation projects on the ground. Through the Initiative, China has contributed its wisdom and resources to implementing the U.N.'s 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. -- The GDI helps build a stronger international consensus on putting development first. We have convened a High-Level Dialogue on Global Development, launched a Forum on Global Action for Shared Development, and held high-level meetings on the GDI at the U.N. Headquarters for four consecutive years. These events have helped make development a central priority on the international agenda. -- The GDI facilitates mutually beneficial development cooperation. More than 130 countries and international organizations actively support the GDI, and they have participated in cooperation under the Initiative. More than 30 GDI cooperation mechanisms and platforms -- such as the Global Development Promotion Center Network and the Global Knowledge Network for Development -- have been established, providing strong support for advancing global sustainable development. -- The GDI helps fulfill the development aspirations of countries in the Global South. More than 2,000 GDI projects, all closely aligned with the needs of beneficiary countries, have brought tangible benefits to the local population. More than 10,000 human resources training programs have been organized to share development approaches and practical skills, helping developing countries to build up their capacity for self-reliant development. Distinguished Guests, Dear Friends, At present, the cause of global development faces grave challenges. The implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development is woefully behind schedule. As a staunch advocate and pragmatic actor in the global development cause, China will work with all parties to practice true multilateralism, advance the implementation of the GDI in greater depth and deliver more substantive outcomes, and ensure that development outcomes benefit more people across the world. To this end, I wish to make four proposals. First, we should strengthen solidarity and coordination to fully implement the SDGs. We should prioritize the implementation of the 2030 Agenda, fully leverage the GDI's role as an accelerator to support the U.N. in strengthening the development pillar, and make policy preparations for the launch of work on the post-2030 global development agenda next September. China is ready to contribute funding to the China-U.N. Trust Fund Project for Statistical Capacity Development to support fellow developing countries in enhancing their statistical and monitoring capacity for implementing the SDGs. Second, we should stay action-oriented and actively pursue development that benefits the people. We should make full use of funding mechanisms such as the China-U.N. Peace and Development Fund and the Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund, and implement more "small and beautiful" livelihood projects that deliver real benefits to local people. China will launch an engineering capacity building program to train 10,000 engineers for developing countries over the next five years. The program will cover areas such as transport infrastructure and information and communications technology (ICT) to help countries improve their infrastructure and strengthen development resilience. Third, we should expand cooperation in priority areas and accelerate empowerment-driven development. We should broaden the scope of GDI cooperation focusing on artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy, new energy, and disaster prevention and mitigation to foster new drivers for sustainable development. China is ready to work with all parties to implement flagship projects under the GDI, including "Digital South" and "Clean Stove," to help Global South countries achieve digital transformation and green development. Fourth, we should strengthen partnerships to promote interconnected development. We should strengthen and expand the Group of Friends of the Global Development Initiative and the U.N. Task Force on Leveraging Partnerships Toward the Implementation of the 2030 Agenda, and conduct extensive cooperation through relevant bilateral, trilateral and multilateral mechanisms to leverage complementary strengths and create synergy. In April next year, China will host the 83rd session of the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) in Shanghai. We will take this opportunity to deepen GDI cooperation with all parties and provide strong momentum for building an Asia Pacific community. Distinguished Guests, Dear Friends, Achieving sustainable development is a shared aspiration of all peoples and an important mission of the United Nations. As the Global Development Initiative marks its fifth anniversary, China will build on this milestone and continue to play its role as a responsible major country. We will work with all countries to strengthen international development cooperation, promote more robust, greener and healthier global development, and make new and greater contributions to building a community with a shared future for humanity. Thank you. ■

item.title: Greener grasslands, smarter farming reshape life on China's pastures
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
HOHHOT, Sept. 26 (Xinhua) -- Across the grasslands of northern China, mornings still begin much as they have for generations: herders check their cattle, feed them and watch for any sign that something may be wrong. For Zhang Weijian, an ethnic Mongolian herder in Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, however, part of that daily routine now involves managing her cattle through an online mini-program on her smartphone. Each of her more than 30 cattle wears an electronic ear tag that can not only monitor its activity but also measure its body temperature. When the temperature rises above 40 degrees Celsius, she can spot the unusual reading on her phone and know it may be time to take a closer look. GOING SMART Zhang, born and raised in Horqin Left Middle Banner in the city of Tongliao, has been using the digital platform for more than two years. "Before, we kept everything on paper. Now I just enter the ear-tag number of one head of cattle on my phone, and its records come up," Zhang said, adding that the records cover breeding and calving history as well as vaccination details. Zhang is among the cattle farmers served by a national modern agricultural industrial park in the banner, one of four such parks in China centered on the beef cattle industry. Established in 2019, the park has so far collected traceability information on over 90,000 head of cattle, accounting for more than 90 percent of total cattle in the park. It aims to track beef cattle throughout the entire production chain, while making agricultural and livestock production more standardized and digitalized. Like Zhang's family, many villagers in the area have long relied on cattle raising for their livelihoods. "Better herd management helps us raise better-quality cattle, reducing losses and increasing our income," Zhang said. Notably, technology is also changing how herders grow and manage the grass that feeds their cattle. At a village in Horqin Right Front Banner, Hinggan League, herder Sainbayar uses quadcopter drones to fertilize his grassland. From June to July, he flies them along preset routes, with three drones taking turns to cover the pasture. "The grass grows better when it gets enough fertilizer," Sainbayar said. The rising pasture yield in recent years has ensured a steady supply of feed for his cattle, while mixers, silage machines and feed conveyors have reduced the manual labor needed to raise them. Inner Mongolia is a major agricultural and livestock production base in China, ranking among the country's top producers of milk, beef, mutton, forage and cashmere. In April 2025, this autonomous region issued an implementation plan for smart agriculture and animal husbandry, setting targets for the development of big-data services, smart farms and digitalization across the agricultural and animal-husbandry industry chain through 2027. The shift toward modern pastoral production is also supported by improvements in infrastructure. Some remote areas deep in the grasslands are located at the end of the power grid, where electricity supplied from afar can fluctuate in voltage, while power outages are not uncommon during snowstorms and strong winds. Recently, a wind-solar-storage microgrid began operating in a village in Chen Barag Banner in the city of Hulun Buir, providing more reliable electricity to 122 herder households. The system uses wind and solar power, along with batteries, to generate and store electricity locally. "Electricity has become much more reliable for us," said Liu Xuebin, a herder in the village. With a stable power supply, his family can now run livestock equipment throughout the day to care for more than 200 cattle and sheep. GREEN PROMISE Across the Horqin sandy land in the autonomous region, stretches of once-bare sand are giving way to trees, grasses and new forms of land use. Located on the northern edge of the sandy land, Horqin Right Middle Banner in Hinggan League is an important area in China's efforts to combat desertification. Its endeavors form part of the three major battlefronts of China's Three-North Shelterbelt Forest Program, a decades-long initiative to curb desertification across northern China. Years of work have continued to improve the local ecological environment. From 2021 to 2025, China treated a total of 152 million mu (about 10.13 million hectares) of desertified land, according to the National Forestry and Grassland Administration. But restoring the land is not simply about planting trees. Increasingly, local efforts are combining ecological restoration with technologies and industries suited to the local environment. At a yellowhorn planting base covering 4,600 mu in a village of the banner, local authorities have partnered with a forestry company to combat desertification via measures including fencing, land leveling, well drilling, drip irrigation and replanting. So far, 308,200 yellowhorn trees have been planted at the base. "It used to be nothing but sandy land here. When the wind blew, sand would fill the air," said Tong Anran, a forestry technician. Yellowhorn, a unique oilseed tree found in China, serves a variety of purposes. "Its seeds can be pressed for oil, its leaves can be made into tea, and its branches can be used for medicinal purposes," said Wang Liwei, the first Party secretary stationed in the village by the Inner Mongolia Academy of Agricultural and Animal Husbandry Sciences. Wang said his research team is exploring processed yellowhorn products to extend the industrial chain and increase the value of the crop. Renewable energy is also being integrated into desertification control. At a photovoltaic desertification-control site in Horqin Right Middle Banner, deep-blue solar panels glint in the sunlight, while plants such as alfalfa sway in the breeze beneath them. Dai Yuliang, an official with the banner's development and reform commission, said the project adopts an ecological restoration model that combines solar power generation with grassland and livestock farming. With an installed capacity of 300 megawatts, the project is expected to generate around 530 million kilowatt-hours of electricity annually, equivalent to saving 159,000 tonnes of standard coal. The project has also encouraged nearby residents to participate through local employment, land leasing and seasonal grass harvesting, creating a model in which solar panels generate electricity, grass grows underneath and desertification control generates income. "Three years ago, this was bare sandy land. Look how well the grass is growing now," said villager Li Jincai, who has also taken part in desertification-control work and earns 200 yuan (approximately 29.63 U.S. dollars) a day. More broadly, in areas covered by the Three-North program, the forestry and grassland industries generated 800 billion yuan in output in 2025. More than 1.5 million farmers and herders have participated in such programs, receiving a total of 10.24 billion yuan for their work. ■

item.title: Giant floral basket installed on Tian'anmen Square for upcoming National Day

Tourists view a giant floral basket installation at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 25, 2026. A giant floral basket has been installed on Tian'anmen Square for the upcoming National Day holiday. Ten sets of three-dimensional flower beds will be arranged along Chang'an Avenue to enhance the festive atmosphere during the holiday. The green spaces on both sides of Tian'anmen Square continue to feature floral ribbons. Additionally, over 7,000 square meters of flowers will be placed along Chang'an Avenue. item.title: China respects U.S. choice on what term to use for artificial intelligence: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
BEIJING, Sept. 26 (Xinhua) -- On what term to use for artificial intelligence (AI), China attaches importance to the position of the U.S. side and respects their choice of the term, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Saturday. The spokesperson made the remarks when answering questions regarding the use of "super intelligence" rather than "artificial intelligence" in the U.S. readout on the outcomes of the just concluded state visit. The two presidents had in-depth discussion on AI during this visit, said the spokesperson, adding the advancement of AI is an ongoing process. "Parties can have more communication and in-depth exchange of views to seek consensus in light of how the process may evolve," the spokesperson said. ■

item.title: Xi's state visit leads to new progress in constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability: Chinese FM
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
BEIJING, Sept. 26 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to the United States has led to new progress in a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said after Xi wrapped up his U.S. visit on Friday. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while briefing reporters on Xi's state visit to the United States from Sept. 23 to 25. President Xi and President Donald Trump had a candid and in-depth exchange of views in a friendly atmosphere of mutual respect on strategic and overarching issues concerning China-U.S. relations and the broader global landscape, Wang said. Since President Trump began his second term, the two heads of state have maintained close exchanges, including three in-person meetings and five phone talks, and fostered a pattern of interaction marked by mutual respect and sincerity, said Wang, noting this has become the most valuable strategic asset in China-U.S. relations. An important political outcome of the visit is that President Xi and President Trump further enriched the substance of the new positioning of China-U.S. relations and have agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, Wang said. Respect means respecting each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respecting each country's choice of social system and development path, and respecting the other side's core interests and major concerns, Wang said. Fairness, Wang continued, means pursuing mutually beneficial cooperation and handling differences through consultation, rejecting a zero-sum game in which one side's gain comes at the expense of the other's, and not seeking unilateral absolute advantage. Reciprocity means that the two countries are equal in sovereignty, that neither side stands above the other, that neither engages in hegemonic nor bullying behavior, that each side's concerns are addressed on an equal basis, and that cooperation across various fields develops in a balanced manner, Wang said. Noting that President Xi has pointed out that a stable China-U.S. economic and trade relationship requires both expanding the list of cooperation and shortening the list of problems, Wang said that the U.S. side should treat Chinese companies fairly, resolve problems through dialogue and negotiations, and promote the sustained, stable and positive development of China-U.S. economic and trade relations. The fentanyl abuse problem in the United States is not caused by China, but China has always acted with the utmost goodwill and made every effort to assist the U.S. side in addressing the fentanyl crisis, Wang noted, adding that the two heads of state tasked the law enforcement agencies of the two countries with continuing to strengthen cooperation and jointly combat transnational crime. To promote people-to-people exchanges between China and the United States, President Xi has announced a series of new measures, including inviting 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchange and study programs over the next five years, Wang said. One piece of good news that has been particularly welcomed by the American public is that two pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will soon arrive at Zoo Atlanta, Wang added. During the visit, Wang said, the two heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on major international and regional issues of common concern and agreed to strengthen coordination to make due contributions to world peace and development. President Xi also encouraged relevant parties to stay committed to peace, supported the United States and Iran in returning to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, resuming dialogue and negotiations at an early date, and ultimately reaching a comprehensive agreement covering the nuclear issue, Wang said. During the visit, President Xi and President Trump also had an in-depth exchange of views on artificial intelligence (AI), pointing out that the two countries should leverage respective strengths rather than guard against each other, Wang said. The two heads of state agreed to make good use of AI dialogue mechanisms between the two countries and jointly prevent the misuse and abuse of AI, Wang added. Noting that this year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials, Wang said that China and the United States are both permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, and it is their shared responsibility to uphold the postwar international order and prevent the resurgence of militarism. China and the United States will respectively host the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Leaders' Summit in the fourth quarter of this year, Wang said, adding that the two heads of state confirmed their mutual support, which will continue to inject momentum into cooperation in the Asia-Pacific and global governance. ■
